title: Priority-path fallback SLI telemetry and visual runbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Instrument a priority-path aware set of token-level SLIs and build a visual dashboard + runbook to guide multi-region failover and circuit-breaker decisions. This ticket focuses on per-request and per-token metrics for premium (priority) vs best-effort traffic, attribution across serving stages (admission queue, batching, KV cache, decode), and creating an ops-friendly playbook for graceful load shedding and regional fallback.
background: We currently have token-level latency SLIs and regional failover dashboards, but they lack clear attribution by priority path and serving stage. Oncall teams need an at-a-glance view to decide whether to trigger capacity failover, adjust admission thresholds, or flip fallback models when p99 token latency increases for premium customers. Existing dashboards are noisy due to per-token cardinality and do not expose the admission/batch/decode split cleanly.
goals: Define and emit priority-path token-level SLIs (p50/p95/p99) with serving-stage attribution
Build condensed dashboard panels that surface root-cause signals for oncall (admission backlog, batch size variance, KV hit rate, model fallbacks)
Provide a runbook with deterministic decision paths for failover and load shedding that reference dashboard thresholds
Keep telemetry cardinality manageable via sketching/sampling and efficient aggregation
out_of_scope: Changes to model code or quantization profiles
Rearchitecting global routing (handled by separate infra epic)
acceptance_criteria: Per-priority token latency SLI emitted (p50/p95/p99) for serving stages: queue_wait, batch_delay, kv_lookup, decode_time
Dashboard contains top-level incident panel with correlated graphs and playbook steps linked
Sampling/sketch strategy reduces telemetry ingestion by >= 70% vs naive per-token streams
Runbook tested via a small chaos exercise that simulates admission backlog and triggers the documented fallback path
technical_design: Emit lightweight spans and counters at four instrumentation points: admission_enqueue_time, batch_release_time, kv_lookup_end, decode_end. Attach minimal routing tags: region, priority_path(premium|standard|best-effort), model_variant, route. Export histograms for token-level latencies using HDR histograms with configurable precision; rollup to p50/p95/p99 and to quantile sketches for long-term retention. Use adaptive sampling: capture 100% of premium tokens, 10% of standard, 1% of best-effort, plus deterministic capture for any token that hits p95+ to avoid survivorship bias. Implement a small aggregation lambda to compute stage deltas and persist daily pre-aggregates for dashboarding. Define thresholds: premium p99 token latency > 400ms for 5m triggers investigation; > 750ms for 2m triggers automated admission tighten and model fallback. Circuit state is derived from admission reject rate, queue_latency, and model error-rate with hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.
data_retention_and_cost_strategy: Store full high-resolution token histograms for premium for 30d, aggregated sketches for standard for 14d, and daily rollups for best-effort for 7d. Use sample weighting on sketches so global aggregates remain unbiased. Implement an ingestion filter to discard expensive traces with small business signal based on route/priority whitelist.

progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed — validated HDR histogram + sketching memory footprint for premium traffic. Trade-off: lower precision for standard reduces ingestion by ~4x.
2026-02-18: Telemetry PR merged (runtime#7892). Added admission_enqueue_time and batch_release_time spans. Started emitting priority_path tag.
2026-02-23: First dashboard draft uploaded. Feedback from SRE: need a combined panel that shows admission_queue_growth + KV-hit drop as correlated signal.
2026-02-27: Chaos plan ready — small-scale admission backlog simulation using synthetic traffic rig. Added test hooks to toggle sampling rates.
2026-03-01: Oncall walkthrough scheduled (2026-03-10). Work remaining: finalize hysteresis values and integrate automated admission tighten action.
risks_and_mitigation: High cardinality risk from per-token instrumentation — mitigated via adaptive sampling and deterministic capture of tail events
False positives from transient GC or infra blips — mitigated by 2-stage threshold with hysteresis and cross-check against infra golden signals
Runbook complexity — mitigate by building a 3-step primary path with optional diagnostics links and automated actions for the most frequent scenario
notes: Design decision: prefer HDR histograms + sketches over storing raw per-token latencies to keep costs predictable
Ops decision: premium traffic must be 100% captured for first 30d after rollout to ensure no blind spots
Follow-up: evaluate whether admission tightener should be run as control plane or per-region agent (separate infra ticket)
